questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving coercion — truthiness.

options.misconception: Confusing the condition with a numeric result
Treating any positive number as false
Assuming the branch prints nothing

questions.explanation: Any non-zero number is truthy, so a value of 1897 enters the first branch and 'yes' is logged. Only values such as zero and empty strings are falsy. Tracing the calls in sequence lands on yes at the console.
questions.hint: Remember which primitive values are falsy in a condition.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving types — typeof.

options.misconception: Assuming the literal is quoted text
Thinking the variable was never set
Confusing a primitive with an object

questions.explanation: typeof reports 'number' for numeric primitives such as 1898. Arrays and objects also report 'object', but a plain integer reports 'number'. Stepping through the code, the final log writes number.
questions.hint: typeof returns a lowercase type name string.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving types — number isnan.

options.misconception: Confusing the test with the value tested
Thinking the conversion throws
Assuming dividing a number by text yields a number

questions.explanation: Dividing 1899 by a non-numeric string produces NaN, and Number.isNaN returns true for that value. The global isNaN would first coerce, which differs from the strict method. Step by step, the final log receives true.
questions.hint: Number.isNaN does not coerce its argument.
